title: Nutrition Q&A #2
summary: NH answers nutrition questions: he rejects 'G-flux' (eating and burning huge amounts of calories), discusses fasting, old-school high-carb diets, coffee dependence, superfoods, water, macros and meal timing on an upper/lower split. Recurring themes are his very low protein intake (50-70 g/day at 210 lb), cutting out milk, recomping at maintenance with patience, and slow bulks over dirty bulks.
claims: NH considers nutrition his weakest area and not very important for natural lifters' pure growth, though essential for health
He likes the Eastern idea that feeding the body feeds disease: eating more means taking in more toxins, and slim elderly Asian populations live long
Gaining weight with age is a Western mindset; being overweight at 50-60 is not normal
G-flux (eating huge amounts and burning them off) still makes your body process massive amounts of food and doesn't improve body composition more than simply not eating the excess
Lifting is great for health but burns few calories; moving the body through space is what burns calories
Fear of catabolism is a myth; the body evolved with food scarcity and strongly preserves muscle, burning fat and other tissue first
Supplement companies pushed the fear of not being fed so people would keep buying shakes and powders
High-calorie diets usually rely on low-nutrient carbs like rice and bread, which don't help body composition
Bulking to 230-240 lb wrecked his appetite and was not fun
He is a minimalist and aims for the smallest protein and calorie intake that still lets him grow
He doesn't fast because going without food makes him unproductive and gloomy; he just avoids long gaps between meals
If you water fast, add vitamins and minerals to the water; dry fasting with no water is stupid and dangerous
Fasting is an extreme fix for earlier overeating; a binge-then-fast cycle means your lifestyle isn't balanced
He follows an old-school high-carb diet: very low fat, with only 60-70 g protein a day (sometimes 50 g) at 210 lb, without losing muscle or strength
Even the low end of the 'optimal' protein range is still higher than he needs
When he swaps carbs for fats he gets fatter; prioritising carbs makes him leaner and more vascular. Test for yourself
Gironda's steak-and-eggs diet, dips and lifting methods are extreme and not for everyone; that many eggs can be dangerous to health
With a weekly fast plus surplus days, what matters is whether the weekly total is a deficit or a surplus
A weekly 24h fast on top of a surplus is not an 'ultimate recomp strategy'; he'd be miserable and prefers eating at maintenance all week
For someone stalled on a cut who can't go below 1900 kcal without misery, switch to a recomp at maintenance now instead of cutting harder
Patience is the number one prerequisite for a successful recomp
Cardio isn't needed for a recomp; it burns calories but can increase appetite, so weigh whether it's worth it
Over-focusing on diet gives subpar results; training is the most important thing
Coffee is addictive; many people can't function without it because caffeine has replaced their natural wake-up hormones, much like steroid users who stop producing testosterone
Take a caffeine break of 1-2 weeks every two months
He is ready to work 15-20 minutes after waking at 7 a.m. without coffee
Superfoods are a marketing meme; some foods are just high in micronutrients, which tend to be the scarce part of a diet
No food makes you shredded or more muscular; that's steroids
Nutrition is mostly zero-sum: you look better from stopping bad foods more than from adding good ones
When he stopped drinking milk his body changed completely: at about the same weight (within 5 lb) he went from watery and soft to defined and vascular
Most supermarket tomatoes and cucumbers have almost no micronutrients because of early harvest and poor soil
Red meat's value lies in its other nutrients, not its protein; egg whites have more bioavailable protein
Examples of superfoods he names: kiwis, garlic, onions, ginger, olive oil
Water guidelines are rough; vegetables and salads supply a lot of water, and he needs little extra water
Judge hydration by urine: clear but not peeing pure water very frequently; follow your doctor if you have a condition
Enough salt and electrolytes are needed to retain water; tap water is poor in minerals
He doesn't count calories or macros; he may leave gains on the table but protects his mental health and still progresses
If you want guidelines, follow science's optimal ranges and experiment within them
Calories in vs calories out governs weight change for everyone, but macros and food choice decide what kind of weight you gain
One-size-fits-all diet advice fails because individuals differ; you must experiment to find what works for you
Eating carbs on press day doesn't directly improve pressing; carbs help pressing only by making you gain weight over time
On an upper/lower split, eat the most carbs (slow-digesting: rice, bread, potatoes) on lower-body days and lean on protein the next upper day for satiety
Lower-body days need more energy; being hungry during heavy squats can kill a workout
You can't recomp forever: below roughly 8-9% body fat, hormones tank and muscle starts to be lost
When a recomp stalls, don't cut deeper; run a very slow bulk, then recomp again
He bulked to 240, dropped to 220, 215, then 210, and began recomping at 210 lb at about 17-18% body fat; he could keep recomping for 3-4 years
Most people carry more fat than they think and quit recomps from impatience; fat doesn't turn into muscle, one is slowly traded for the other
Any surplus adds fat and water; dirty bulks mostly add fat and better leverage, not muscle
Bulk surpluses can be well under 10%; slow increases give better long-term progress
Research claiming you need a 25% surplus to build muscle seems poorly done to him
viewer_questions: G-flux high intake and high expenditure
weekly fast plus surplus for recomp
stalled cut: recomp now or later
